record.original_question: Let Γ be the first Grigorchuk group, viewed inside its profinite completion PF(Γ). Determine whether there exists an element g in PF(Γ) but not in Γ such that the subgroup ∆ generated by Γ and g has the congruence subgroup property. Producing such an element would give a new example of a non-isomorphic inclusion ψ: Γ -> ∆ whose induced map on profinite completions PF(ψ) is an isomorphism.

evidence.quote: Open problem. Let Γ be the first Grigorchuk group; it is an infinite group which is residually a finite 2–group, and all its proper quotients are finite 2–groups.
The problem is to find an element g in the complement of Γ in PF(Γ) such that the subgroup ∆ of PF(Γ) generated by Γ and g has the congruence subgroup property.

This would provide one more example of a homomorphism ψ : Γ −→ ∆ which is not an isomorphism and which would be such that the homomorphism PF(ψ) is an isomorphism, namely one solution to the original Grothendieck problem of a different nature than the existing ones (from [PlaTa–86], [PlaTa–89], and [BriGr–04]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Γ denote the first Grigorchuk group, that is, the group generated by the four automorphisms a, b, c, d of the infinite rooted binary tree defined by Grigorchuk; Γ is infinite, residually a finite 2-group, and every proper quotient of Γ is a finite 2-group. Let PF(Γ) denote the profinite completion of Γ, so that Γ embeds densely in PF(Γ). A subgroup H of PF(Γ) is said to have the congruence subgroup property if every finite-index subgroup of H contains the closure (in PF(Γ)) of some level stabilizer St_Γ(n), where St_Γ(n) is the subgroup of Γ fixing the n-th level of the binary tree pointwise.

Question: Does there exist an element g ∈ PF(Γ) ∖ Γ such that the (abstract) subgroup Δ := ⟨Γ, g⟩ ≤ PF(Γ) generated by Γ together with g has the congruence subgroup property?

(Equivalently, exhibit such a g, thereby producing an inclusion ψ : Γ ↪ Δ which is not an isomorphism but for which the induced homomorphism PF(ψ) : PF(Γ) → PF(Δ) of profinite completions is an isomorphism.)
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., works on the true prosoluble completion of the Grigorchuk group and on pro-C congruence properties for groups of rooted-tree automorphisms, including a 2024 note on Grothendieck pairs dedicated to Grigorchuk) continues to discuss this construction without reporting a solution. No source found announces the existence of such an element g or rules it out, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The true prosoluble completion of a group: Examples and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: An open problem asks to find an element in the complement of the Grigorchuk group in its (pro-2/prosoluble) completion such that the generated subgroup has the congruence (subgroup) property.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as an open problem in surveys on completions of the Grigorchuk group.

status_evidence.title: Some remarks on Grothendieck pairs (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Grothendieck pairs in connection with the Grigorchuk group, without reporting resolution of the cited open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is still discussed as a target rather than as solved.
